terra.problem: The explanation gives a reason God starts with Jerusalem's origin that the text does not provide.
The partial-score joke makes light of the newborn's neglect.
The text says no one cared enough to perform the listed acts of compassion; it does not say no one cared enough to keep her.
Her parents are mentioned again in Ezekiel 16:45, so saying they never come up again is incorrect.
Saying Jerusalem isn't going anywhere adds a claim the text does not make.
Papa says his whole look is a hat, although he also wears an apron and neckerchief and stands on his gold base.
The text says God bestowed the splendor; it does not say Jerusalem did not earn it.
The text says Jerusalem trusted in her beauty, but does not say she looked at herself instead of at God.
Saying it was her past she forgot, not a list of names, asserts what she did not forget. The text does not say that.
The text names public squares and street heads but does not say they were among the busiest spots in town.
The cookie comparison makes light of the serious unfaithfulness being described.
She never gets there goes beyond the text, which says she was still not satisfied after turning to the Assyrians.
Sending them away wasn't on her mind assigns Jerusalem a thought the text does not give.
No jokes from me comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
Nothing she built stays standing goes beyond the mounds and shrines the verse says will be destroyed.
They aren't protecting anything is broader than the text, which says they will destroy the mounds and shrines.
The text says Jerusalem paid her lovers, but does not say she had been paying them the whole time.
